Dispatching now rather than waiting for a triage grading pass: the design landed 30 minutes ago, the lane has no other dispatchable card (its three queue items are all blocked on other seats), and the standing maintainer directive is to keep dispatching. Triage remains free to grade this card — including `target:v17` — while it is in flight; nothing in the dispatch depends on that grading.

⛔ **Not re-opening the design.** D9 is ratified. Any disagreement with it is a new ADR amendment, not a decision for the implementing dev.

The card body carries the full constraint set. The three that a naive implementation gets wrong (owner-contributor artifact identity, the `own`-gated provisioning that must become base-layer-gated, and #6995's three bindings) are named there and are all repeated in the dispatch as hard requirements, each with its own pin.

## os-dev report

**Issue**: #7277 · **PR**: #7306 (draft) · **Branch**: `claude/issue-7277-adr-0029-d9-overlay-layer` · **Base**: `origin/main` @ `708431313` · **Status**: done · **Premise still valid**: yes

D9's premise was re-verified against `origin/main` before any edit: the two hydration seams still pass two arguments (so `ownership` defaults to `'own'`), `registerObject`'s same-package splice still removes the packaged contributor, `getArtifactItem`'s object branch still reads the merged body, `provisionPrimary` is still gated on `own`, and `ObjectOwnershipEnum` still has zero runtime consumers. Only the line numbers had moved.

### 1. The bit-for-bit resolution check

The pin compares two registries directly: D9 (packaged `own` + tenant `overlay`) against the pre-D9 world (the overlay body as the sole `own` — what the splice left behind), with `expect(d9.getObject(name)).toEqual(preD9.getObject(name))`. **No resolved schema moved anywhere**, `_provenance: 'org'` included. The pin is not decorative: RV-3 below turns it red, which is what "the resolved object moved" actually looks like.

### 2. The three naive-failure pins

1. **`getArtifactItem` reads the OWNER contributor.** Implemented via a new private `resolveOwnerLayer(fqn)` — the owner's declaration with its extenders folded on, ignoring the overlay layer. What comes back is the code-layer baseline, which is what every consumer of `lookupArtifactItem` wants (`_lock` / `_packageId` / `_provenance` grafting, the `code` baseline layer); with no overlay registered it is byte-for-byte the previous answer, pinned separately. Uncached on purpose so it cannot drift from `mergedObjectCache`'s seven invalidation points.
2. **The provisioning gate is now "is this a BASE layer"** (`own` or `overlay`). Worked from D9 section 5's blast-radius table, not from grep — dispositions in section 5 below.
3. **#6995's three bindings** implemented as ruled: same package normal, package-less sentinel accepted, different package refused at the producer with the newly minted `OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH` / 422 and counted in `loadMetaFromDb`'s per-record `errors` at boot.

### 3. Late install — measured, then implemented

D9's recommended default is taken: the code layer becomes owner, the tenant contribution is re-classified as its overlay layer. Narrowed to fire only when the sitting owner is tenant-authored (`_provenance: 'org'`) and the incoming body is not — two code packages claiming one name is still D3's cross-package refusal, pinned.

The measurement found a second spelling the card did not name: when the arriving package's id **equals** the row's binding, pre-D9 did **not** throw "already owned by" — it took the re-registration splice and destroyed the tenant's customization silently. Both spellings are pinned. A useful side effect: a boot order that puts `loadMetaFromDb` before package registration now self-heals into the same two layers.

### 4. What happened to #7012's guard — RETIRED, measured

RV-5 put the guard **back**, unchanged in intent, and exactly **one** test turned red: `a package-bound RUNTIME-authored object is retired, and its data plane closes`. Nothing that protects a package-shipped object moved at all.

That is the whole argument. After D9 the packaged `own` contributor is never spliced out, so `isArtifactBacked` is honest and the case the guard was written for cannot reach the retirement limb (the layer subtraction returns first, and the predicate is true besides). What the guard still reached was only its own **accepted cost** — a package-bound RUNTIME-authored object (Studio's package workspace, #4636) kept listable-but-rowless until restart. With the predicate honest that is no longer the cheap direction, it is the wrong answer: nothing ships the name, the row WAS the item, and data CRUD kept writing into a table whose metadata the operator had just deleted.

Also verified for assumption 2: `removeObjectOverlay` **cannot** live in tier 3. Tier 1 (`removeRuntimeShadow`) returns as soon as it heals the generic metadata map, so an object whose plain-key shadow it can heal would keep its overlay layer registered — the #6808 asymmetry replayed one layer down. The subtraction runs ahead of the tier walk, unconditionally for `object`.

### 5. Blast-radius table dispositions (D9 section 5, row by row)

| D9 row | Disposition |
|:--|:--|
| `registry.ts` default priority | third arm added, `DEFAULT_OVERLAY_PRIORITY = 150` |
| `provisionPrimary` / `provisionSearchCompanion` | gate changed to `own` **or** `overlay`; pinned by the `nameField` test AND (unexpectedly) by the bit-for-bit test |
| second-owner throw | now unreachable from the overlay seams; still thrown for a second code package (pinned) |
| same-package `own` splice | untouched; the overlay never enters this branch. Late install added ahead of it |
| same-package `extend` splice | mirrored for `overlay`, keyed by KIND not package (D9.9) |
| base selection | `find(overlay) ?? find(own)`, extracted into a shared `foldExtenders` |
| extender fold | unchanged |
| `getAllObjects` `_packageId` stamp | **no code change needed** — it already reads `getObjectOwner`, which now naturally yields the packaged owner. Pinned |
| `getObjectOwner` | unchanged; doc states it still means "owns the table" |
| `assertSingleOwnerPerObject` | count literally unchanged; orphan-overlay violation class added |
| `unregisterObjectsByPackage` | the overlay layer leaves with the owner it layers over |
| `unregisterObject` | extender guard unchanged; the layer-addressed verb runs first in the heal |
| `getArtifactItem` object branch | reads the owner layer (D9.6) |
| `spec/data/object.zod.ts` | third value + the "loader-set, never authored" clause |
| `protocol.ts` both seams | D9.8 discriminator via `getPackagedObjectOwner` |
| `objectql/src/plugin.ts` two seams | discriminator adopted, with a **narrower** rule: a body arriving under the owner's own id and not claiming tenant provenance stays `own`, so a package's HMR reload is not mistaken for a layer |

`ObjectContributor` is exported, so the widened union is a public type change — minor, with a changeset, as D9 says.

### 6. Reverse verification — direction decided before each run

Every probe reverts to this PR's own base; `dist` is rebuilt before any result is read.

| Probe | Predicted | Measured | Reading |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| RV-1 `getArtifactItem` back to the merged body | 5 red | **6 stable red** + 1 unstable | Missed prediction: the late-install pin also asserts the predicate is honest — cause identified. The unstable one is GREEN at `--maxWorkers=1` and in isolation under the same probe; reported as an ordering artefact, **not counted as evidence** |
| RV-2 base selection back to `own` | 6-8 red | **11 red** | Under-predicted |
| RV-3 provisioning gate back to `own` only | **exactly 1 red** | **2 red** | Missed one, and it is the valuable one: the **bit-for-bit pin** goes red. Skipping title provisioning on the overlay layer MOVES the resolved schema |
| RV-4 both seams back to `'own'` | ~9 red, all in the e2e file | **exactly 9 red, 0 in the registry unit file** | Hit, including the prediction that the registry unit file is immune (it registers `'overlay'` directly) |
| RV-5 #7012's guard put back | **exactly 1 red** | **exactly 1 red** | Hit — the measured basis for the retirement |

**Green in both directions, reported as guards not evidence**: the single-owner count on an overlaid object; the cross-package second-owner refusal; the artifact item still carrying extenders when there is no overlay; a tenant re-writing its own runtime object staying a single `own`; package-less and non-installed-binding objects still being retired; non-object types untouched by the mismatch rule.

**Unmeasured**: none. The unstable RV-1 red is reported as unstable rather than counted as passed.

### 7. CI — per-job conclusions on `426cf5281`

- **ESLint** — `completed` / **success** (this is where the repo's family gates run)
- **TypeScript Type Check** — `completed` / **success**
- Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core (1/3, 2/3, 3/3) and the roll-up, Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3, 2/3, 3/3) and the roll-up, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, Console Pin Freshness, Check Documentation Links, Auto Label — all `completed` / **success**
- **ADR maintainer approval — `completed` / failure, BY DESIGN.** The PR touches `docs/adr/0005-*.md` (the "Amended by" pointer this card scoped). The gate's own message: *"Drafting this PR was fine and stays fine — only the MERGE is reserved."* Green path is an APPROVED review from @hotlong, which re-runs the check. Nothing to fix here.

Local: `objectql` 168 files / 2974 tests, `metadata-protocol` 67 / 861, plus the consumption-radius sweep (`metadata` 30/593, `runtime` 118/1837, `rest` 76/1219, `plugin-security` 43/878, `cli` 105/1139) — all green. The suites that actually **exercise the changed path** are `objectql` and `metadata-protocol`; the other five are breadth, and that is stated rather than counted.

### 8. Two things needing your attention

**a. CROSS-SEAT: two `packages/spec` files touched.** The dispatch says to stop and report if `packages/spec` is needed. Both edits are required verbatim by D9.1 (`ObjectOwnershipEnum` gains `'overlay'`) and D9.9 (the ADR-0112 code), and D9.1 explicitly rejects the alternative of a parallel local union ("one vocabulary, not a parallel list", Prime Directive #8) — so the card cannot be implemented as ratified without them. I implemented rather than stopping, and declare it here for routing. Measured against #6298's own admission criterion: `ObjectOwnershipEnum` has no runtime consumer in this repo, so widening it changes **no metadata's legality** — what parsed before parses byte-for-byte after, and what was rejected stays rejected.

**b. D9.6's cost reaches one gate the record does not name.** Confirmed that `saveMetaItem` now refuses an overlay write to a packaged object every time (pinned, three attempts, asserting `code` AND `status`). **The same predicate also feeds `deleteMetaItem`'s two-tier authorization and `SysMetadataRepository.assertAllowed`** — so RESETTING such a customization is refused too, and the repository check is topology-independent, so a control-plane kernel refuses as well. Not softened: both are pinned, since a fixture encoding the old leniency would be encoding the defect. The hatch is the same one door (`OS_METADATA_WRITABLE=object`), now required for the LIFE of the customization rather than only its first save. D9.6 states this for the save side only; the delete side is the same declaration on the other verb, and it is exactly the delete whose unchecked version took the object off the data plane (#7012). Flagging in case the maintainer wants a separate ruling on the reset path.

Not absorbed: #6725 (the write side, `domain:engine-core`). Not touched: `content/docs/releases/`. `content/docs/references/**` (12 files) are regenerated artifacts — the whole diff is the new error code count plus the ledger and object pages.

No out-of-scope findings were filed: nothing surfaced that was not already covered by D9's own record or by this card.
